Vegan Mushroom Soup

From casual to elegant, this creamy Vegan Mushroom Soup is rich, velvety comfort in every spoonful. Packed with earthy mushrooms and layered with savory flavor, it’s a dairy-free mushroom lovers’ delight!

If you’ve ever craved that classic cream of mushroom soup but wanted it vegan, lighter, and homemade, this is it. It comes together fast, packs fantastic flavor, and has an oil-free option. Brimming with umami, this recipe has quickly earned a permanent spot in our rotation!

VEGAN MUSHROOM SOUP

Why You’ll Love This Recipe!

  • It’s quick and easy (start to finish in 40 minutes!), perfect for a weeknight dinner.
  • You likely have most of the ingredients on hand; you’ll just need the mushrooms and optional wine.
  • It cooks in one pot for minimal cleanup!
  • The hardest part is slicing the mushrooms, but you can cheat and pick up pre-sliced for ease and convenience.

Without further ado, let’s make something wonderful!

Ingredients You’ll Need

Creamy mushroom soup from scratch has a depth of flavor that’s healthy and so much better than canned soups, thanks to fresh ingredients and herbs. Here’s what you’ll need, plus easy swaps so you can make it your own (no matter what’s in your kitchen).

  • Mushrooms — Fresh cremini (brown baby bella) mushrooms give a nice earthy, rich flavor. I’ve had great results with a mix of cremini and white button, or even adding shiitake, oyster, or portobello for extra umami and texture.
  • Non-Dairy Butter — I use vegan butter (my favorite is Miyoko’s) for a rich flavor, but feel free to use olive oil or water for an oil-free version.
  • Wine — My secret ingredient is a vegan dry white or red wine, which adds complexity. Check Barnivore to confirm it’s vegan-friendly. Feel free to skip it; your soup will still be delicious!
  • Aromatics — Yellow onion and fresh garlic build the savory base. White onion works in a pinch for a slightly milder flavor. No fresh garlic? Swap in 3–4 teaspoons garlic powder (add it later to avoid burning).
  • Herbs — Fresh thyme and parsley are my go-tos and complement the mushrooms perfectly. Dried works too. Swap with herbes de Provence, Italian seasoning, rosemary, tarragon, oregano, basil, or chives based on what you love or have on hand.
  • Coconut Milk — Full-fat or coconut cream adds richness without a coconutty flavor. Feel free to use low-fat coconut milk instead. If you don’t care for coconut or want to keep it low in fat, swap with non-dairy milk or my Vegan Cream.
  • Vegetable broth — I prefer low-sodium veggie broth or Better Than Bouillon (Amazon affiliate link), mixed with water, for the most control over sodium.
  • Optional cornstarch — If using a lighter milk, use the slurry option to thicken, stir it in toward the end, and simmer until thickened. Arrowroot powder is a great 1:1 sub.

***Prefer the recipe card? You’ll find the exact measurements and instructions just below.

How to Make Vegan Mushroom Soup

This easy soup comes together effortlessly with just a handful of steps and about 40 minutes total. Here is a quick overview with photos for reference (plus, who doesn’t love to see a big pot of beautiful sautéed mushrooms!).

Sauté: Heat oil (or do an oil-free water sauté with 1/4 cup water) in a large pot. Add the onions and garlic, cooking until softened and aromatic, about 5 minutes. This builds the savory foundation!

Add the mushrooms & wine: Toss in the sliced mushrooms and thyme with a splash of optional dry wine. Cook until the mushrooms release their juices, about 5–7 minutes.

Simmer: Pour in the vegetable broth, cover askew, and simmer gently for 15 minutes. In the last 5 minutes, stir in the coconut milk (or your fave sub) so it heats through without curdling.

Thicken & finish: If you want extra body, stir in the optional cornstarch slurry and simmer briefly until thickened, about 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat, mix in fresh parsley, and taste, adjusting salt & pepper as needed.

That’s it, simple and delicious — enjoy!

Quick Soup Tips

For a thicker, bisque-style soup, reduce the broth to 3 cups.

Blended Version: For a classic velvety texture, transfer about half (or all, depending on how chunky you like it) to a blender and purée until smooth, then return to the pot. Or use an immersion blender right in the pot.

Season well: Mushrooms need enough salt, and a little extra pepper helps!

Serving Suggestions

This mushroom soup shines on its own, but pairs well with a simple side for a hearty, satisfying dinner. Here are some of my favorite pairings:

  • Bread: Serve with a slice of artisan bread, soft & chewy naan, or gluten-free socca flatbread to soak up the juices. Crusty bread is classic and is perfect for scooping up chunks of mushrooms!
  • Salad: A classic house salad or a simple leafy green salad topped with vegan ranch, lemon-herb hemp dressing, or flax & evo balsamic vinaigrette is light, refreshing, and completes the meal.
  • Grain: For extra heartiness, stir 1/4–1/2 cup brown or white rice, farro, or quinoa into your serving bowl.

How to Store Leftovers

Mushroom soup stores and reheats perfectly, making it great for meal prep. The flavors even deepen after a day or two!

It keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Give it a quick stir before serving, as plant-based soups can separate slightly when chilled (but it blends right back together beautifully).

Reheat on the stovetop (my preferred method). Warm over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally until warmed through. Add a splash of broth or milk to loosen it up as needed. Alternatively, heat in the microwave in short bursts, stirring every 30 seconds to heat evenly and avoid hot spots.

Can I Freeze Mushroom Soup?

Yes! It freezes wonderfully for up to 3 months. My favorite way is to portion into single servings in freezer-safe containers or silicone molds (affiliate links) — great for grabbing just what you need! To freeze, let cool completely and leave about 1 inch of headspace at the top for expansion. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

VEGAN MUSHROOM SOUP

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star

5 from 52 reviews

  • Author: Julie | The Simple Veganista
  • Total Time: 40 minutes
  • Yield: Serves 4 – 6 1x
  • Diet: Dairy-Free, Vegan
Print Recipe
Pin Recipe

Description

From casual to elegant, this deliciously creamy vegan mushroom soup is dairy-free, easy to make, and a mushroom lover’s delight!

Ingredients

Units Scale
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, vegan butter (I love Miyoko’s), or 1/4 cup water for oil-free
  • 1 large yellow onion, diced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 lbs. mushrooms (cremini or white), sliced
  • 1/2 cup vegan dry white wine (red ok too), optional
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme or 1 1/2 teaspoons dried
  • 4 cups vegetable broth
  • 3 tablespoons cornstarch or arrowroot (+ 1/4 cup water), optional
  • 1 can (14oz.) coconut milk (full-fat or cream) or 1 1/2 cups vegan cream or unsweetened cashew milk (*see notes)
  • mineral salt & fresh cracked pepper (or white pepper), to taste
  • 1/4 cup parsley, chopped

Instructions

  1. Sauté: In a large pot, heat oil or water over medium heat; sauté the onions and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms, thyme, and wine; cook for 5 minutes.
  2. Simmer: Add the broth, bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 minutes. In the last five minutes, add the coconut or plant milk and cook for five more minutes.
  3. Blend for creaminess (optional): For a classic velvety texture, transfer about half (or all, depending on how chunky you like it) to a blender and purée until smooth. Return to the pot, or use an immersion blender right in the pot (if you blend, you can skip the cornstarch slurry).
  4. Slurry (optional): Mix the cornstarch with cool water. Add to the soup and stir frequently for 2-3 minutes, until the soup thickens slightly.
  5. Remove from heat and stir in the parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
  6. Serve warm with homemade Artisan Bread or Naan to soak up the juices and swipe up every last bit of goodness!

Notes

Store: Keep leftovers in the refrigerator for 4-5 days; store covered. To keep longer, store in freezer-safe containers or baggies for up to 2-3 months.

Instead of thyme, try Herbes de Provence.

*To keep this recipe low-fat, use light coconut milk or unsweetened plant milk of choice, and make sure it’s at room temperature so the soup can heat back up quickly. You may want to puree part of the soup or use a cornstarch slurry to add body and volume.

Vegan wine: Check whether your favorite wine is vegan or find a new one at Barnivore.

  • Cook Time: 30 min
  • Category: Dinner, Soup
  • Method: Simmer
  • Cuisine: American
